auth.description: Bitbucket Cloud Access Token, sent as a bearer token. A Workspace Access Token is valid for exactly one workspace, which is the same boundary this connector's pinned `workspace` describes; scope it to repository:read plus pullrequest:write for the writes below
auth.name: bitbucket.access_token
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: Create one in the workspace's settings under Security -> Access tokens -> Create Workspace Access Token, with the Repositories: Read and Pull requests: Write scopes. Bitbucket shows the token once. Create it in the same workspace you name below, so the token reaches no further than this connection does
config.label: Bitbucket access token
config.name: access_token

config.help: The workspace this connection manages, as its slug — the single path segment right after bitbucket.org/ in any of its URLs. In https://bitbucket.org/acme-engineering/widget-service the workspace is acme-engineering, not acme-engineering/widget-service and not the full URL. Find it under Workspace settings -> Overview. One connection manages one workspace
config.label: Bitbucket workspace
config.name: workspace

description: Bitbucket Cloud repositories and pull requests for one pinned workspace: list the workspace's repositories, read one, list and read its open pull requests, open a pull request, comment on one, and approve one

operations.description: List the repositories in this connection's workspace, with each one's slug, name, description, main branch and privacy. Takes no argument at all: the workspace is pinned when the connection is made, so this reads exactly the workspace the operator chose and no other. Returns Bitbucket's first page only; this connector declares no page or filter parameters, and the response's `next` field carries the URL of the following page. The `slug` returned here is what every other operation in this connector takes as `repo_slug`. Also this connector's `verify`: a bounded read that runs unattended and needs nothing beyond the token and the pinned workspace

next.description: The URL of the next page, absent on the last one. This connector cannot follow it — see its header note on pagination

pagelen.description: How many values a page holds; 10 by default

size.description: The total number of repositories, when Bitbucket computes it

full_name.description: `workspace/slug`. Note that this is two segments: `repo_slug` is the second one alone

has_issues.description: Whether the repository's own issue tracker is enabled

is_private.description: Whether the repository is visible only to the workspace

language.description: The primary language Bitbucket detected, empty when it detected none

links.description: Bitbucket's hypermedia links for this repository, including `html.href` — the page to give a human

mainbranch.description: The default branch — the `destination_branch` most pull requests target

project.description: The Bitbucket project grouping this repository. Left untyped rather than enumerated

slug.description: The repository's URL segment — pass this as `repo_slug` to every other operation here

uuid.description: The repository's stable identifier, in braces. Survives a rename, which `slug` does not

operations.description: Read one repository in this connection's workspace by its slug, with its main branch, privacy, project and size. Use it to confirm a repository exists and to learn its default branch before opening a pull request against it

params.description: The repository's URL segment, from bitbucket-repository-list's `slug` — the part after the workspace in a Bitbucket URL. Not the `workspace/slug` pair Bitbucket calls a full name
params.name: repo_slug

links.description: Bitbucket's hypermedia links, including `html.href` — the page to give a human

mainbranch.description: The default branch — the branch a pull request usually targets

owner.description: The account owning the repository. Identifies a named person for a personal workspace — read it for what the calling flow needs and do not persist it beyond that

project.description: The Bitbucket project grouping this repository. Left untyped rather than enumerated

uuid.description: The repository's stable identifier, in braces

operations.description: List the open pull requests on one repository in this connection's workspace, newest activity first. Returns OPEN pull requests only — that is Bitbucket's default and this connector declares no `state` parameter to change it (see its header note), so merged and declined pull requests are not returned. Returns Bitbucket's first page only; the response's `next` field carries the URL of the following page. Each value's `id` is what bitbucket-pull-request-get, -comment and -approve take

params.description: The repository's URL segment, from bitbucket-repository-list's `slug`
params.name: repo_slug

next.description: The URL of the next page, absent on the last one

pagelen.description: How many values a page holds; 10 by default

author.description: The account that opened it. Identifies a named person — read it for what the calling flow needs and do not persist it beyond that

close_source_branch.description: Whether merging will delete the source branch

description.description: The pull request's body, as Markdown

id.description: The pull request's number within its repository — what the other pull-request operations address it by

links.description: Bitbucket's hypermedia links, including `html.href` — the pull request's page, the link to give a human

state.description: OPEN, MERGED, DECLINED or SUPERSEDED. Always OPEN here, because this call declares no state filter

operations.description: Read one pull request by its number, including its description, its source and destination branches, its current state and who is participating. Reads a merged or declined pull request too, unlike bitbucket-pull-request-list

params.description: The repository's URL segment, from bitbucket-repository-list's `slug`
params.name: repo_slug

params.description: The pull request's number within its repository, from bitbucket-pull-request-list's `id` — the number in its Bitbucket URL
params.name: pull_request_id

author.description: The account that opened it. Identifies a named person — read it for what the calling flow needs and do not persist it beyond that

description.description: The pull request's body, as Markdown

id.description: The pull request's number within its repository

links.description: Bitbucket's hypermedia links, including `html.href` — the link to give a human

merge_commit.description: The commit the merge produced, null while the pull request is open

participants.description: Everyone who has touched the pull request, each with their `approved` flag and `role`. Left untyped rather than enumerated; this is the field bitbucket-pull-request-approve writes into

reason.description: Why it was declined, empty otherwise

reviewers.description: The accounts asked to review. Left untyped rather than enumerated

operations.description: Open a pull request from one branch to another in a repository of this connection's workspace. Both branches must already exist and be pushed. Bitbucket does not deduplicate: opening the same source-to-destination pull request twice creates two of them, and notifies the repository's watchers twice. The created pull request, with its assigned `id`, is in the response

params.description: The repository's URL segment, from bitbucket-repository-list's `slug`
params.name: repo_slug

params.description: The pull request's title, as it will read in the list. Bitbucket requires one
params.name: title

params.description: The branch holding the change, exactly as it is named in the repository — the branch this pull request would merge from
params.name: source_branch

params.description: The branch the change would merge into. Bitbucket's own default is the repository's main branch, which bitbucket-repository-get returns as `mainbranch.name` — name it explicitly rather than assuming it
params.name: destination_branch

author.description: The account the token belongs to. Identifies a named person — read it for what the calling flow needs and do not persist it beyond that

close_source_branch.description: False unless the repository defaults it otherwise; this connector does not set it

id.description: The new pull request's number — what bitbucket-pull-request-comment and -approve address it by

links.description: Bitbucket's hypermedia links, including `html.href` — the new pull request's page, the link to give a human

state.description: OPEN on a pull request just created

operations.description: Add a top-level comment to a pull request. The comment is attributed to the account the token belongs to and notifies everyone participating; Bitbucket sends no un-notification, so a comment posted in error can be deleted but not un-seen. This posts a general comment on the pull request, never an inline comment on a line of the diff

params.description: The repository's URL segment, from bitbucket-repository-list's `slug`
params.name: repo_slug

params.description: The pull request's number, from bitbucket-pull-request-list's `id`
params.name: pull_request_id

params.description: The comment text, as Markdown. Bitbucket renders it and returns the rendered HTML alongside the raw text
params.name: body

content.description: The comment as stored and as rendered

id.description: The comment's id within the pull request

links.description: Bitbucket's hypermedia links, including `html.href` — the comment's anchor on the pull request page

user.description: The account the comment is attributed to — the token's own. Identifies a named person; read it for what the calling flow needs and do not persist it beyond that

operations.description: Approve a pull request as the account this connection's token belongs to. This records a review that a human may not have performed, and in a repository with an approval merge check it can release a merge that gate was configured to hold — treat it as an assertion about a review, not as a bookmark. Bitbucket answers a repeat approval with 409 rather than approving twice. Sends no body: the approver is the token's own account

params.description: The repository's URL segment, from bitbucket-repository-list's `slug`
params.name: repo_slug

params.description: The pull request's number, from bitbucket-pull-request-list's `id`
params.name: pull_request_id

role.description: PARTICIPANT or REVIEWER — how the token's account relates to this pull request

user.description: The account the approval is attributed to — the token's own. Identifies a named person; read it for what the calling flow needs and do not persist it beyond that
